1.title: Amazon DynamoDB for Applications
1.text: Welcome to Module six: Amazon Dynamo D B for Applications. It covers the exam area Domain one: Development with A W S Services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. The data model. Reading data. Capacity. Indexes and other features. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain one: Development with A W S Services (thirty percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: The data model
1.text: The data model. Amazon Dynamo D B is a managed, serverless No sequel key-value and document database with single-digit-millisecond latency. Table. A collection of items. Item. One record (up to four hundred K B). Attribute. A field; items in a table need not share attributes. Partition key. Decides which partition stores the item; required. Sort key. Optional; items with the same partition key are ordered by it. Primary key. The partition key, or partition key plus sort key.

1.title: The data model, continued
1.text: The data model. The figure shows this: Dynamo D B keys: partition key, sort key and indexes.

1.title: Choosing keys
1.text: Choosing keys. A good partition key is high-cardinality (many distinct values) so requests spread evenly. A hot partition happens when one key gets most of the traffic (a date, a status flag, a popular item). Exam tip: "Uneven load on one partition" equals choose a higher-cardinality partition key, or add a suffix to spread writes.

1.title: Reading data
1.text: Reading data. Get Item. What it does: One item by full primary key. Cost: Cheapest. Query. What it does: Items with one partition key value, optionally a sort key condition. Cost: Efficient. Scan. What it does: Reads the whole table. Cost: Expensive; a filter expression applies after the read, so you still pay for all items scanned. Use projection expressions to return only some attributes, and handle pagination with Last Evaluated Key.

1.title: Read consistency
1.text: Read consistency. Eventually consistent (default). May return slightly stale data; half the cost. Strongly consistent. Returns the latest write; costs more; not available on global secondary indexes. Transactional. All-or-nothing reads and writes across items (higher cost).

1.title: Capacity
1.text: Capacity. On-demand. Unpredictable traffic; pay per request. Provisioned. Predictable traffic; set read and write capacity units, optional auto scaling. One read capacity unit (R C U) equals one strongly consistent read up to four K B per second (or two eventually consistent). One write capacity unit (W C U) equals one write up to one K B per second. If you exceed capacity you get Provisioned Throughput Exceeded Exception: retry with backoff.

1.title: Indexes and other features
1.text: Indexes and other features. Local secondary index (L S I). Same partition key, different sort key; created with the table only. Global secondary index (G S I). Any partition and sort key; has its own capacity; eventually consistent only. Conditional writes. Write only if a condition holds; implements optimistic locking. T T L. Automatically delete expired items by a timestamp attribute (Module seven). Streams. Ordered change records, read by Lambda. D A X. In-memory cache in front of Dynamo D B (Module fifteen). Batch and transactions. Batch Get Item and Batch Write Item (up to one hundred reads and twenty-five writes); Transact Write Items for all-or-nothing. Exam tip: Eventually consistent reads cost half; strongly consistent reads are not available on a global secondary index.

1.title: Indexes and other features, continued
1.text: Indexes and other features. Exam tip: Query and Get Item are the efficient reads; Scan reads the whole table and a filter expression does not reduce the capacity you pay for.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A table uses "order date" as the partition key and all writes go to today's value. What is the problem? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A hot partition. A low-cardinality, time-based key concentrates writes on one partition.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A developer must look up all orders of one customer, newest first. Which design fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Partition key Customer Id and sort key Order Date, then Query. Query on a partition key with a sort key returns related items in order efficiently.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An application needs the latest data right after a write. Which read mode should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Strongly consistent on the table. Strongly consistent reads return the latest write, but not on a G S I.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team must query the table by an attribute that is not part of its key. What is the best option? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A global secondary index on that attribute. A G S I provides an alternate key for queries.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Two clients update the same item and one overwrites the other. How can the developer detect this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A conditional write using a version attribute. Conditional writes implement optimistic locking.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. An application has unpredictable traffic and the team wants no capacity planning. Which capacity mode fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: On-demand. On-demand scales automatically and bills per request.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the maximum item size? Answer: four hundred K B. Question two. Which is cheaper, Query or Scan? Answer: Query. Question three. What does one R C U provide? Answer: One strongly consistent read of up to four K B per second (or two eventually consistent reads).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which index type must be created with the table? Answer: A local secondary index. Question five. Can a G S I serve strongly consistent reads? Answer: No, only eventually consistent. Question six. What does a conditional write enable? Answer: Optimistic locking and safe updates.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Keys: partition ( plus sort); high cardinality avoids hot partitions. Reads: Get Item, Query (efficient), Scan (whole table, filter after). Consistency: eventual (default, cheaper), strong (not on G S I), transactional. Capacity: on-demand versus provisioned; R C U four K B, W C U one K B. Indexes: L S I (table creation, same partition key), G S I (any key, eventual).
